**Finding: compliant (preferred position) — no redline.**

The Agreement contains no most-favoured-nation obligation running against AP:

- **Searches run:** "most favored nation", "no less favorable", best-terms/rate-card/pricing-offered-to-others, right of first refusal / match. All returned nothing.
- **Commercial terms reviewed:** Section 5 (Fees and Payment) is a revenue-share referred out to Exhibits, with no benchmarking or price-parity covenant; Section 3(j) (Winning Bid Price) sets a floor *in AP's favour* ("no less than the minimum price that Customer has agreed to accept"), not an MFN burden.
- **Direction confirmed:** Section 1 expressly preserves AP's freedom to sell Inventory via other agents or directly to third parties, reinforcing that no better-terms/matching mechanic binds us.

Preferred element "Customer has no most-favoured-nation obligation benefiting Vendor" is already met, so we take no position beyond noting that any future Exhibit pricing should be checked for parity language before signature.
